SOUTH-SOUTHEAST OF YOKOSUKA, JAPAN, HAS TRACKED NORTHEASTWARD AT
20 KNOTS OVER THE PAST SIX HOURS. ANIMATED MULTISPECTRAL SATELLITE 
IMAGERY (MSI) DEPICTS A RAPIDLY DETERIORATING SYSTEM, WITH A NOW FULLY 
EXPOSED LOW LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC) ON THE SOUTHWESTERN 
PERIPHERY OF AN AREA OF CONVECTION WHICH IS DEVELOPING INTO A DELTA 
RAIN REGION, INDICATIVE OF THE RAPID ONSET OF EXTRATROPICAL TRANSITION 
(ETT). THE MSI ALSO DEPICTS STRONG WARM FRONTOGENESIS OCCURRING IN THE 
NORTHEASTERN SECTOR OF THE CIRCULATION. THE SYSTEM IS CURRENTLY MOVING 
ACROSS THE 26C ISOTHERM AND ENTERING AN AREA WITH SIGNIFICANTLY COOLER 
SSTS. THE INITIAL POSITION IS ASSESSED WITH HIGH CONFIDENCE BASED ON 
THE EXPOSED LLCC IN THE MSI. THE INITIAL INTENSITY IS ASSESSED WITH 
LOW CONFIDENCE, HEDGED HIGHER THAN THE BULK OF THE SUBJECTIVE AND 
OBJECTIVE INTENSITY ESTIMATES IN PERSISTENCE WITH AN EARLIER SYNTHETIC 
AP
